system.name: Sirius
system.one_liner: a system that composes multiple, order-conflicting network-function chains from edge-cloud business traffic onto one P4-capable gateway ASIC

content.key_idea: An edge cloud's business traffic maps to several network-function chains whose module orderings conflict (SNAT-IN reverses SNAT-OUT's order), so Sirius composes them onto one custom P4 gateway ASIC with multiple recirculating pipelines instead of one monolithic program.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three sub-figures: (a) edge cloud topology, (b) three chains with checker/VxLAN/session/acl/switch modules in conflicting orders, (c) the gateway's internal ASIC pipelines and NIC/CPU path.

evidence: We designed and built our own P4-capable edge gateway

the gateway is equipped with a programmable switch ASIC and server-grade CPU with dozens of cores

summary: This three-panel figure introduces Sirius's problem setting and gateway design. Panel (a) shows an edge cloud's topology: redundant P4-capable Gateways sit at the border between commercial switches/servers and the backbone network, absorbing several types of business traffic. Panel (b) shows three example network-function chains built from shared P4 modules (checker, VxLAN, session, acl, switch): VPC-VPC uses three modules, while SNAT-OUT and SNAT-IN use the same five modules but in different, partly reversed orders, illustrating the ordering conflicts Sirius must resolve when composing chains onto one program. Panel (c) shows the gateway's internal architecture: a programmable switching ASIC with four parallel pipelines and a traffic manager that recirculates packets, fed by external 100G Ethernet ports and connected through a non-programmable NIC and PCIe to a server-grade CPU.
